summary:
Second G3 English review of EFMP-302 Unit 4 (ADR-0019 section 2, cycle 2 of 2), run in a fresh
session by a reviewer that neither drafted nor translated these bytes. All 137 bound inputs were
digest-verified against the prepared run-002 manifest at commit 4ae0952 with zero mismatches, and the
recomputed bound set matched the manifest exactly with no extra or omitted file. The reviewed content
tree was clean at the start and at the end of the review.

Disposition is escalate. Two independent grounds, one carried forward and one newly determinate.

First, the carried ground. The unit's primary document, the National Professional Standards for
Teachers in Pakistan (2009), is still not bound into the bundle and is still unretrievable from this
host: itacec.org returned 401 and nacte.org.pk 404 on an independent re-attempt this session, while
ERIC answered 200 in the same session. The UNESCO / International Task Force global framework is
likewise unretrievable (403 from unesdoc and from teachertaskforce.org). The ten standard names, the
three-part internal division, the 2009 Ministry of Education origin and MCQ-04's key therefore remain
corroborated only across secondary sources. The author's "## Unverifiable sources" declaration is
honest and accurate, and the unit now carries a visible caveat inside fig-U4-4 and an instruction to
the tutor in the teacher notes, which is creditable mitigation; it is not verification. Under the
review skill a reference not in the bundle cannot silently support an accepted decision, so this needs
a bundle that binds the document or an owner ruling on the standing of secondary corroboration.

Second, the new ground. The Isore repair is real but incomplete, and the incompleteness has produced
internal contradiction. This reviewer re-fetched the ERIC PDF, confirmed its sha256 matches the bound
excerpt exactly, re-extracted the text independently, and verified every quotation. The explanatory
passages at topic-04.mdx:94-99, topic-03.mdx:111-115 and topic-01.mdx:142-146, and the fig-U4-8 SVG,
now represent Isore correctly, including that she calls the purposes "often conflicting - but not
necessarily incompatible". Run-001 findings [1] and [2] are resolved at those locations. But the
pre-repair strong claim survives in seven other places that the repair did not reach, including the
unit summary, two "Check your understanding" questions, two self-assessment checklist lines, the RRQ-4
mark scheme and the fig-U4-8 figure-manifest row. The result is a unit that teaches "It is not a proof
that one document can never do both" and then, on the same page, asks the learner to explain why one
document cannot do it, and a mark scheme that awards a mark for the claim the body disclaims. That is
not a residue of the old defect; it is a new, self-contradictory state created by the partial repair,
and it cannot be resolved by re-running a review on unchanged inputs.

Genuine progress is recorded. All eight figures now exist, render, carry meaningful alt text, and swap
to dark variants correctly under data-theme - run-001 findings [5] and [6] are resolved on the render
side, verified by actual Chromium inspection rather than by a green gate. The two false concept-graph
links are gone: the licensing linkage [8] is fully resolved, and RRQ-02 was widened so sub-topic U4-02
is now genuinely touched by an item. The ERQ rubric tables are now keyboard-reachable scrollable
regions with an announced aria-label, resolving [13]. The MCQ option permutation preserved key
correctness: all ten keys were re-derived independently from the prose and all ten agree.

Six blocking and two uncertain findings are unresolved. Four run-001 findings are resolved, one is
partially resolved, one is superseded by a sharper determinate form, and ten remain open.

This report is advisory. It is unsigned; no qualification record or protected registry entry exists for
this reviewer; nothing here certifies the unit, activates a reviewer, writes a tracker row, or
constitutes sign-off.

findings.message: Isore repair incomplete: the pre-repair claim survives in seven locations and now contradicts the corrected body. topic-04.mdx:94-99 teaches that Isore calls the purposes "often conflicting - but not necessarily incompatible" and that this "is not a proof that one document can never do both". Still asserting the opposite: (1) topic-01.mdx:183-184 CYU Q5 "cannot fully be the same document"; (2) topic-01.mdx:210-211 checklist "cannot be the same document"; (3) topic-04.mdx:160 CYU Q2 "cannot be well served by one document"; (4) topic-04.mdx:176 Summary "two purposes with incompatible requirements"; (5) unit-assessment.mdx:43-44 Unit summary "requirements are incompatible in one document"; (6) unit-assessment.mdx:209-210 RRQ-4 mark scheme awards its final mark for "one document cannot hold both sets of requirements"; (7) specs/content/efmp-302/figures/unit-04.md fig-U4-8 row, whose Prompt and Alt text columns both still read "incompatible in one document" and now diverge from the committed SVG and from the alt text at topic-04.mdx:72. REPAIR: bring all seven to the strength the body and the source support, in one pass. Verified against the ERIC full text re-fetched and hash-matched this session.

Primary source still unavailable and unbound: npst-pakistan-2009. Independently re-attempted this session - itacec.org HTTP 401, nacte.org.pk HTTP 404, while files.eric.ed.gov answered 200 in the same session, so this is a per-host access condition. The document is not in the run-002 prepared manifest. Claims still unverified against it: the ten standard names at topic-02.mdx:74-83 and the whole content of fig-U4-4; the knowledge/dispositions/performance division at topic-02.mdx:54-56 and fig-U4-3; the 2009 Ministry of Education origin with UNESCO and USAID support at topic-02.mdx:41-43 and topic-01.mdx:104-106, which is also MCQ-04's key. Mitigation is creditable but is not verification: fig-U4-4 renders a visible "navigational summary, not the standards themselves ... Read it in the primary document" caveat, and unit-teacher-notes.mdx:29-33 tells the tutor to check the names. REQUEST: prepare a bundle that binds a copy of the primary document, or record an owner decision on the standing of secondary corroboration. Do not resolve by re-running the review on unchanged inputs. Carried unresolved from run-001 finding [0].

Source unverifiable: unesco-teacher-ethics (UNESCO / International Task Force on Teachers, 2019, Global framework of professional teaching standards). Independently re-attempted - unesdoc.unesco.org HTTP 403 and teachertaskforce.org HTTP 403, while ERIC answered 200 in the same session. Unverified claims: topic-01.mdx:86-87, that the framework was published to give countries a common reference point, and the scope / granularity / stakes axes at topic-01.mdx:92-96 on which national frameworks are said to differ - which is now also the content RRQ-02's added clause assesses. REQUEST: bind a retrievable copy or an equivalent citable text into the next bundle. Carried unresolved from run-001 finding [3].

Citation traceability still broken for goe2008. specs/content/efmp-302/coverage/unit-04.md grounds U4-07 (topic-02.mdx "### Indicators, and how a domain is evidenced in practice") and U4-09 (topic-03.mdx "### Building evidence against an indicator") in goe2008, and specs/content/efmp-302/sources/unit-04.md line 51 records the same, but "Goe" appears nowhere in topic-02.mdx or topic-03.mdx - the only occurrence in the unit is topic-04.mdx:233. sources/unit-04.md:4-5 still asserts "every key here is cited in prose and in a per-topic `## Further reading` section", which remains false for this key. The full text was re-fetched and hash-matched this session and DOES support the substance relied on ("Multiple measures - each designed to measure different aspects of teacher effectiveness - must be employed"; "Consider the purpose for the evaluation of teacher effectiveness before deciding on the appropriate measure to employ"), so the repair is to cite it where it is used: add it to Further reading in topics 4.2 and 4.3 and attribute the multiple-measures and match-the-measure-to-the-purpose points in prose. Carried unresolved from run-001 finding [4].

Two mark schemes now conflict with their own repaired stems. (a) RRQ-02 at unit-assessment.mdx:120-122 was widened to add "and name one way national standards frameworks differ from one another" - which is what makes sub-topic U4-02 assessed and makes the CON:EFMP-302-4-4 -> RRQ-02 concept link true - but its mark scheme at unit-assessment.mdx:199-201 still reads "(6 marks) Two marks per instrument" across the three instruments only. The added requirement carries zero marks and no marking guidance, so U4-02 is assessed in the stem and unrewarded in the marking. (b) RRQ-04 at unit-assessment.mdx:127-129 was rewritten to ask "what a system must decide in advance if it wants one document to serve both", presupposing that it can, while its mark scheme at unit-assessment.mdx:207-210 still awards its fourth mark for concluding "that one document cannot hold both sets of requirements". A candidate answering the question as asked loses a mark; one contradicting the repaired topic-04.mdx:94-99 earns it. REPAIR: re-point both mark schemes at what the stems now ask.

The alt text does not enumerate the evidence examples, so the clipped content is not recoverable from the accessibility tree. (b) fig-U4-8 (topic-04.mdx:72) - inside the orange summary bar, line 2 occupies y=371.9..384.5 and line 3 y=381.9..394.5, overlapping by 2.6px; the source uses 10px leading at y=382 -> y=392 against 18-20px elsewhere in the same figure at the same 11px font-size. The colliding lines are precisely the text carrying the corrected Isore qualification, which is this cycle's headline repair.
